key_insight: Language models exhibit nonlinear dynamics across three clocks—network depth, training steps, and generated tokens—linking behaviors such as instability and repetition to established dynamical-systems concepts.
engineering_relevance: Reduced-order dynamical models offer interpretable tools for studying training stability and choosing generation temperatures that balance coherence with escape from repetition.
method: Synthesize about 200 papers into a Three-Clock Dictionary, labeling correspondences as proved, measured, or conjectured.
Derive mechanical and statistical models of softmax, gradient descent, attention, loss spikes, and repetition loops.
Test predictions on open language models using a laptop CPU.
evidence_signal: Experiments on GPT-2 and Pythia support Arrhenius-law escape from repetition with logit-gap barriers; Pythia layers become more expansive during training, while a small transformer trains at a multi-mode edge of stability.
watch_item: Escape-based controllers remove repetition loops but do not yet outperform the best fixed temperature, and not all proposed dynamical correspondences are proved.
paper_title: Large Language Models as Nonlinear Dynamical Systems: The Three Clocks of Depth, Training, and Generation
